notes:
- **New: a built-in reference library for every Minecraft version**: the app now ships with version-exact modding guides for 131 loader and version combinations - every Forge release from 1.7.10, every NeoForge release from 1.20.2 and every Fabric release from 1.14, up to the newest 26.x versions, plus Quilt from 1.18.2 to 1.21.1. The guides cover setup, items and blocks, entities, events, networking, data and client code, and the classes, imports and method names in them were checked against the real game and loader files of that exact version. The Assistant reads the guides for your project's version before it writes, so a Forge 1.12.2 mod, a Fabric 1.20.1 mod and a NeoForge 26.3 mod each get the right names, imports and file formats. The library is on your PC and works offline.
- **The Assistant looks things up while it works**: when it isn't sure how a class or method looks on your version, it now checks the reference library in the middle of its answer - where a class moved, what it was renamed to, which methods really exist - instead of guessing. This takes no extra steps from you.
- **New: Auto-Healer - build errors fixed without AI first**: **Run Mod** and **Build** now check your JSON files and mod id before compiling, then repair common errors by themselves - missing imports, renamed classes and the well-known API changes between versions (like `ResourceLocation` on 1.21 and newer) - up to 3 times, using no tokens. Only what is left goes to the Assistant, with an exact report of each error and the line it is on, so its repairs are faster and cheaper. Every file the Auto-Healer changes is backed up in your project's `.mycraftingai/heal-backups` folder. Turn it on or off in **Settings > Assistant > Repair without AI first**.
- **Repairs use your version's own files**: when the app looks up the names in a failing build, it now reads only the libraries of your project's Minecraft version - never classes from another version you have installed - so suggested fixes always match your project.
- **Only versions with verified guides in the version lists**: the new-project screen and the Version Converter's targets now list only Minecraft versions that have their own guides in the reference library - 52 for Forge, 14 for NeoForge and 45 for Fabric - still matched against the loader's live list of builds. The note under the list says how many are available. The Version Converter's target versions are picked from the list, so a conversion always starts from verified guides. The version of the mod you convert *from* can still be anything.
- **Fabric on Minecraft 26.x**: Fabric dropped Yarn names after 1.21.11, so Fabric 26.x projects and conversions now use Mojang's official names, the way Fabric's own tools do.
